milestone.title: CPD L5 evidence audit: detect same-session cross-role hand-offs on a milestone

intent.outcome: After this ships, an `mp reviews l5-check <id>` command reads a milestone's persisted hand-off records (M133's data shape) and reports same-session, cross-role hand-off violations as a structured advisory. The check integrates into `mp validate` so a `make validate` run includes the L5 audit. The hand-off recording (mp reviews handoff) reads session identity from the `MP_SESSION_ID` and `MP_SESSION_ROLE` env vars when present, falling back to the existing manual --from-session / --to-session flags. Result: the L5 rule (manifesto principle 13 + L5 session-boundary law) becomes auditable per-milestone. The check is advisory by design — it can detect same-explicit-session-id reuse, not 'the human ran coordinator and runner in the same opencode window.' Team discipline remains the real enforcement.

problem.description: M119 (agent role dispatch + skill registry) and M133 (review handoffs data shape) shipped the role-token surface (mp agent role) and the hand-off persistence (mp reviews handoff with from_session / to_session / data / evidence). But there is no command that audits whether a milestone's hand-off records actually respect the L5 rule. A milestone can be marked 'done' with hand-offs that all came from the same session id and the same role — the rule is documented in the manifesto (line 369: 'cross-role stage transitions never share a session') and the data is persisted, but nothing checks the data. The team is dogfooding CPD right now and the runner is the same human-operator as the coordinator in many sessions; the discipline works because the human is honest, not because the toolkit catches violations. The L5 check makes the rule auditable: the data is already there, the check is a 100-line read-side command. Auto-injection of session identity (MP_SESSION_ID, MP_SESSION_ROLE) lets the harness pre-populate the fields the agent would otherwise have to type — a small ergonomics win that raises the floor on accidental violations (the agent can't forget to declare a session id if the harness does it for them). The check stays advisory: enforcement would require session identity the agent cannot forge, which is a separate design discussion and out of scope for this milestone.

in_scope: Data-shape prerequisite (additive): add from_role: String and to_role: String fields to the M133 ReviewHandoff struct (crates/mp-model/src/milestone.rs), with #[serde(default)] so pre-M142 records round-trip as empty. The current M133 shape has only free-form from_session/to_session with no structured role, so the role_inversion AC (AC-05) and the role_inversion violation class below cannot otherwise be implemented. MP_SESSION_ROLE env var populates these (see env-var item). This is a small additive model change, not a reshaping of the existing fields.

New `mp reviews l5-check <id>` subcommand: reads the milestone's hand-off records (M133 data shape), groups them by stage transition (4→5, 7→8, 8→9, 9→10 per the mp-handoff skill's 4 hand-off points), and detects violations. A violation is: hand-off N's from_session equals hand-off N+1's to_session AND the stage transition is cross-role (e.g. runner's stage 7→coordinator's stage 8 is a cross-role rotation; that rotation should have a session boundary — i.e. to_session != from_session in the role sense).

Output shape: { ok: bool, violations: [{ at_handoff: handoff_id, from: handoff_id_or_role, to: handoff_id_or_role, reason: string, severity: 'advisory' }], summary: { total_handoffs, cross_role_handoffs, violations } }. ok: true with empty violations when clean; ok: false (advisory, not blocking) when violations exist. The command exits 0 either way; the caller decides what to do with the report.

Violation reasons (deterministic, three classes): (a) 'same_session_across_role_boundary' — from_session == to_session at a cross-role hand-off; (b) 'missing_session_identity' — either from_session or to_session empty (or the matching from_role/to_role empty); (c) 'role_inversion' — from_role/to_role contradict the receiving stage's expected role (e.g. hand-off 8->9 is runner-receives, so to_role must be 'runner'; to_role='coordinator' is a role_inversion). Role is read from the new structured from_role/to_role fields, not parsed out of the free-form session string (which carries no reliable role signal).

Integrate the L5 check into `mp validate` as a non-blocking sub-check: when a milestone is in the validate scope, the l5-check runs and its violations appear in the validate output under an 'l5_audit' section, with severity 'advisory' (not 'error'). make validate does not exit non-zero on advisory violations.

Env-var auto-injection in mp reviews handoff: if MP_SESSION_ID and MP_SESSION_ROLE are set in the environment, they pre-populate from_session / to_session AND the new from_role / to_role fields (MP_SESSION_ROLE fills the role of the recording side; the to_role is the complement per the stage-transition table). Manual --from-session / --to-session and new --from-role / --to-role flags override the env vars (operator escape hatch).

Session identity contract documented in `mp reviews handoff --help`: MP_SESSION_ID is a stable string the harness sets per session (opencode, pi, Cursor, Claude Code each pick their own format — opencode uses conversation id, pi uses a UUID, etc.). MP_SESSION_ROLE is one of 'coordinator' | 'runner' (matches `mp agent role`). The contract is 'forgeable by humans, auditable by review' — this milestone is honest about that.

Tests: l5-check on a fixture milestone with clean hand-offs returns ok: true; on a fixture with same-session cross-role hand-off returns ok: false with the right violation; on missing-session-identity returns ok: false with the right reason. Env-var auto-injection: MP_SESSION_ID + MP_SESSION_ROLE set → handoff records the env values; --from-session flag overrides. make validate runs the l5-check on a fixture and surfaces the advisory in the report.
Docs: update `mp reviews handoff --help` with the env-var contract and a one-paragraph note in the `mp reviews` subcommand help pointing at the manifesto L5 rule.
out_of_scope: Forging-resistant session identity (signed tokens, harness-side trust, OS-level session isolation). The session id remains a string the agent can type. Real L5 enforcement is a separate design discussion; the manifesto itself calls single-agent mode 'the minimum viable CPD' (manifesto §503-515) and accepts that L5 is degraded discipline. This milestone is the audit trail, not the enforcement.

Auto-injecting MP_SESSION_ID from inside `mp` itself. The harness owns session identity; `mp` reads it. A future milestone can ship harness-side integration that writes the env var, but this milestone only does the read side.
Blocking the milestone on L5 violations. The check is advisory by design — blocking would break single-agent mode entirely. The team gets a warning; the human decides whether to honor it.

Migrating the existing `mp-handoff` skill content into `mp-flow` (that's M141). This milestone assumes M141 has either landed or is in flight; the L5 check reads the persisted hand-off data, not the skill content.

Per-stage session identity (recording which session handled stage 5, stage 6, stage 7 separately). Today's hand-off records are per-transition (4→5, 7→8, 8→9, 9→10). The L5 check works on transitions; finer-grained per-stage logging is a future extension if the data shape grows.

Auto-l5-check on `mp milestone complete` (i.e. fail the complete command if L5 violations exist). Same reason as #3 — blocking breaks single-agent mode. The check is a separate command the operator runs explicitly or that runs as part of `mp validate`.

Bulk L5 audit across all milestones in the plan. The check is per-milestone today; a future `mp reviews l5-check --all` (or equivalent) is a small extension. The current milestone is the per-milestone primitive.
